standard.title: Cohesion through nominalisation and connectives
standard.description: investigate a range of cohesive devices that condense information in texts, including nominalisation, and devices that link, expand and develop ideas, including text connectives
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how cohesion devices including overviews and paragraph structure guide readers (AC9E7LA04). They have not yet examined nominalisation as a condensing device or the range of text connectives that signal logical relationships between ideas.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how nominalisation condenses information and how text connectives link, expand and develop ideas across extended texts.

nodes.label: Text connectives and logical relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify text connectives and explain the logical relationship each signals — conclusion, reason, expansion, condition.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify text connectives in an argument or explanation and explain the logical relationship each signals (e.g. causal, conditional, additive).
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how text connectives structure an argument's logic across a full text — sequencing, supporting and qualifying claims — using examples including 'therefore', 'moreover', 'since', 'because', 'if … then'.
wider: Compare how the same logical relationship is signalled differently in academic versus journalistic texts (e.g. formal connectives vs implicit logical flow)
Analyse how a writer's choice of connective can shade the logical force of a claim (e.g. 'however' vs 'nevertheless' vs 'despite this')

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a repertoire of connective types (causal, conditional, additive, contrastive, conclusive) to see text connectives as a system rather than isolated vocabulary items. Recognition across diverse texts is the goal.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least three text connectives in a text and categorises the logical relationship each signals
Student explains how the connectives shape the reader's understanding of how ideas are linked

nodes.label: Nominalisation as condensing device
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify nominalisations and explain how they condense prior information into a noun phrase that advances the text's argument or explanation.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two nominalisations in a text and explain what information each condenses and how this allows the text to move forward.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate nominalisation across academic and technical texts, analysing how abstract nouns condense clauses or arguments, distil information and allow the text to treat that information as a given as it develops.
wider: Compare nominalisations in scientific and humanistic writing, examining differences in how each discipline uses condensing to build knowledge
Analyse how nominalisation can obscure agency and examine the ideological implications of this choice in journalism or political discourse

response_modes.reason: Nominalisation is hard to see in familiar contexts because it feels natural. Exposure to academic and technical texts from different disciplines helps students recognise nominalisation as a systematic device rather than an occasional quirk. Cross-discipline examples resolve the 'is this even a device?' confusion.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Nominalisation connects to register, power and ideology — the observation that nominalisations hide agency (e.g. 'the decision was made' vs 'she decided') is genuinely enriching for Y9 and connects directly to critical literacy. This is substantive width, not mere extension.
success_criteria: Student identifies a nominalisation and states what process or clause it condenses
Student explains how condensing allows the text to carry that information forward as an established premise

nodes.label: Cohesive devices as a system
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how nominalisation and text connectives work together as a cohesive system, allowing extended texts to develop complex arguments while maintaining coherence.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how nominalisation and at least one connective type work together in a text to condense and link ideas across paragraphs.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how a range of cohesive devices — nominalisation, text connectives, and their interaction — work together to sustain and develop an argument or explanation across an extended text.
wider: Analyse a complex argumentative text to map how nominalisations are introduced, carried and linked across sections, tracing the cohesive architecture of the whole
Compare the cohesive density of a student text with a published text, identifying where cohesive devices are underused and what effect this has on coherence

response_modes.reason: The final node requires students to see nominalisation and text connectives as coordinated devices that together achieve cohesion — not independent items on a checklist. The integration of how condensing and linking work together is the analytical target.

success_criteria: Student explains how a nominalisation and a connective in the same text jointly contribute to cohesion
Student shows how the devices allow the text to carry an argument or explanation across multiple paragraphs
